labeling_note: This taxonomy defines labeling rules. It does not claim that every processed case has been manually labeled.

intents.name: delivery_issue
intents.description: A shipment is late, missing, delayed, incorrectly tracked, or has a delivery-time problem.
inclusion_criteria: The main problem is when or whether a package will arrive.
The customer reports a missing, late, delayed, or apparently delivered shipment.
exclusion_criteria: Use order_issue when the problem is changing, cancelling, or placing an order without a delivery-status problem.
Use refund_return when the main request is money back or returning an item.

examples.text: Is your company bound to destroy people's diwali celebration? You can't deliver a package ever after 5 days of expected delivery
It's all good now and it turns out the tracking shows it was never delivered. Your rep = v helpful and replacement is on its way

intents.name: order_issue
intents.description: The customer needs help placing, changing, cancelling, or correcting an order or its contents.
inclusion_criteria: The request concerns an order action or an incorrect item/order.
The customer wants to change or cancel an order before the main issue becomes a refund request.
exclusion_criteria: Use delivery_issue when the central issue is shipment progress or arrival.
Use product_seller_issue when the central issue is seller authenticity, product price, or seller behavior.

examples.text: I just inadvertently bought a Kindle book on my account when I wanted to buy it as a gift, anyway I can change this?
I preordered amazon echo but want to go for amazon plus now. Anyway to reach out to seller?

intents.name: refund_return
intents.description: The customer asks for a refund, reports a missing refund, or wants to return an item.
inclusion_criteria: The requested outcome is money back or a product return.
The customer says a promised or expected refund has not arrived.
exclusion_criteria: Use payment_billing when the problem is a charge or payment method and no refund/return is the main request.
Use delivery_issue when the customer only reports a late or missing shipment.

examples.text: Order id in India not solved refund issue since four months by amazon India
I already connected. Did live chat, you are ready for refund.

intents.name: payment_billing
intents.description: The customer reports a charge, payment-method failure, invoice problem, or unexpected billing.
inclusion_criteria: The message focuses on payment authorization, a charge, an invoice, or billing.
The customer reports an unexpected Prime or order charge.
exclusion_criteria: Use refund_return when the customer explicitly wants money returned.
Use order_issue when the payment mention is incidental to a broader order change.

examples.text: I tried to sign up for a Prime trial but I think it's automatically charged for the year!!
Able to place order, but then a few hours later I'm advised to Update My Payment Method. My card is valid and has funds on it!

intents.name: account_prime
intents.description: The customer needs help with account access or Prime membership features and status.
inclusion_criteria: The main problem concerns login, password, account access, or account settings.
The customer asks about Prime membership status or benefits without a specific billing problem.
exclusion_criteria: Use payment_billing for an unexpected membership charge.
Use digital_technical when the problem is a product or application malfunction rather than account access.

examples.text: This is after package was supposedly out for delivery this morning. What am I paying for Prime for?
Prime lists/sells at higher than MRP. Caught. Now bribing me with Rs.100 voucher.

intents.name: digital_technical
intents.description: The customer reports a problem with a digital product, device, application, media, or technical feature.
inclusion_criteria: The issue concerns Kindle, Fire TV, Prime Video, an app, downloads, playback, or a broken digital feature.
The customer reports a technical error or a feature that does not work.
exclusion_criteria: Use account_prime when the central problem is login or membership access.
Use order_issue when the problem is an accidental purchase or order action rather than a malfunction.

examples.text: Sign up page appears broken. Cannot sign up. Help!
Does Kindle support Kannada (Unicode rendering) now?

intents.name: product_seller_issue
intents.description: The customer reports a product-quality, authenticity, pricing, or third-party seller problem.
inclusion_criteria: The message alleges a counterfeit, duplicate, defective, or incorrect product.
The message focuses on product price, seller behavior, or contacting a seller.
exclusion_criteria: Use delivery_issue when the central problem is shipment timing.
Use refund_return when the requested outcome is primarily a return or refund.

examples.text: Amazon now sell duplicate product. I bought Biotique Basil And Parsley Soap and they send me duplicate product.
Difference between best possible prices and charging higher than MRP.

intents.name: other_unclear
intents.description: The message is too vague, mainly feedback or complaint, or does not fit another intent with enough confidence.
inclusion_criteria: The customer provides insufficient detail to identify a specific support problem.
The message is general feedback, thanks, or a complaint without a clear requested action.
exclusion_criteria: Do not use this label when a more specific intent is supported by the customer's main request.

examples.text: Thanks. Think I'll just chance it. Frustrating as the route must be sorted so someone somewhere knows when it will arrive approx just not me
